name: China economy
summary: China's October factory output rose 4.8% and retail sales 0.4%, both below forecasts; Q3 growth 4.5%
state: Statistics bureau data released on 16 Nov showed October industrial output up 4.8% a year, below the 5.3% forecast, and retail sales up 0.4%, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January–October (Business Standard; Quartz). Third-quarter growth was 4.5%, at the bottom of the 4.5–5.0% range analysts expect for the year. No new developer default wave or financial contagion was found as of 17 Nov, so Normal holds with momentum weakening.
for_you: Weaker Chinese demand tends to weigh on commodity exporters and firms selling into China. No financial contagion has been reported.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 growth 4.5%, near target; no developer default wave or contagion found

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
